title: Galatians Bible Quiz - Chapter 4
description: Ten questions on Galatians 4: the heir who was like a bondservant, the Spirit crying Abba Father, the writer's first preaching among them, and the allegory of two covenants.

questions.text: To whom is the heir compared while he is still a child?
questions.explanation: The chapter says that so long as the heir is a child he is no different from a bondservant, though he is lord of all.

answers.text: To a bondservant
To a hired worker
To a stranger in the house
To a guardian of the estate

questions.text: How is the Son described when God sent him out in the fullness of the time?
questions.explanation: It says that when the fullness of the time came, God sent out his Son, born to a woman, born under the law.

answers.text: Born in the wilderness
Born of the free woman
Born to a woman, born under the law
Born an heir of Abraham

questions.text: What does the Spirit of his Son cry in the hearts of the children?
questions.explanation: It says that because they are children, God sent out the Spirit of his Son into their hearts, crying, Abba, Father.

answers.text: Holy, holy, holy
Abba, Father
Amen and amen
Maranatha

questions.text: What does the writer say they are observing?
questions.explanation: After asking why they turn back to the weak and miserable elemental principles, he says they observe days, months, seasons, and years.

answers.text: Fasts and solemn vows
Feasts and sacrifices
Oaths and tithes of grain
Days, months, seasons, and years

questions.text: How does he say they received him, even though his flesh was a temptation to them?
questions.explanation: He says they did not despise or reject him, but received him as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.

answers.text: As an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus
As a stranger passing through
As a teacher of the law
As one of their own countrymen

questions.text: What does he testify they would have done for him if possible?
questions.explanation: He testifies that, if possible, they would have plucked out their eyes and given them to him.

answers.text: Followed him all the way to Arabia
Sold all their possessions for him
Plucked out their eyes and given them to him
Gone with him to Jerusalem

questions.text: Until what does he say he is again in travail for his little children?
questions.explanation: He calls them his little children, of whom he is again in travail until Christ is formed in them.

answers.text: Until he can come to them
Until the law is fulfilled
Until they are circumcised
Until Christ is formed in them

questions.text: What does the chapter say is written about Abraham's two sons?
questions.explanation: It says it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the servant and one by the free woman.

answers.text: That both were born through promise
That one was by the servant and one by the free woman
That both were heirs of the covenant
That the younger was sent away

questions.text: Which of the two covenants in the allegory is said to be Hagar?
questions.explanation: It says these are two covenants, and the one from Mount Sinai, bearing children to bondage, is Hagar.

answers.text: The covenant from Mount Sinai, bearing children to bondage
The covenant of the Jerusalem that is above
The covenant made with the free woman
The covenant of promise given to Isaac

questions.text: What does the chapter quote the Scripture as saying about the servant and her son?
questions.explanation: It quotes the Scripture as saying to throw out the servant and her son, for the son of the servant will not inherit with the son of the free woman.

answers.text: That they should be blessed as well
That they should wait for the appointed day
That they should be thrown out, for he will not inherit
That they should be counted as children of promise
